utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with co-counsel Ms. Patricia Sellers and our case manager Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink. And also good morning to Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And good morning to you, Mr. Wubben, and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. We have with us today our legal assistant Ms. Adisa Mehic and our case manager Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. I hope you all had a good weekend and enjoyed the sun and the warmth, the weather we had over the weekend here. Any preliminaries before we bring in the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And to start with your remark, the Prosecution didn't feel like a good weekend. This weekend has as an outcome a decision-making that is rather disappointing for the Prosecution. We decided not to call this witness. We decided not to call this witness because for two days of proofing showed us that this witness was not cooperative in giving his information as we put questions towards him, and he is not -- and that's also the outcome of the -- of this evaluation. He will not be supportive to the strategy of the Prosecution to prove our case. That means, and that's why it's disappointing, that we projected this witness as being an important witness, an insider witness. We scheduled the witness accordingly. We -- he had given two statements to the Office of the Prosecutor, and thus we were indeed confident to go forward with him recently, in August last year, but yet these are events that might happen, and we regret to say that indeed we will not call him as a witness today. We regret also the aspect of the projected days that we scheduled him as a witness, and we will try to reschedule as much as possible, though that will be a huge effort, and also, with a view to the rights of the Defence, to prepare any new witnesses, that we reschedule them at the end of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you, Mr. Wubben. Are there any remarks from the Defence bench?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have nothing to say in relation to this. This is entirely up to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes. I agree with you. It's entirely something that we cannot involve ourselves with, except that -- anyway, least said, better, better it is. What's the position now? How can we -- because this witness was scheduled to testify the entire week between Prosecution and Defence, and -- we have a responsibility, which I'm sure you appreciate, to try -- to try to make the best possible use of the time we have if it is at all possible. I do acknowledge that there are or may be problems because witnesses don't fall from heaven. I mean, you have to arrange for their transportation, proofing, and they also have to arrange for their being away and travelling. So -- and not to mention the problems that the Defence might encounter if they are put in a position where they have to deal with a witness before they were prepared to. So I definitely have in mind, of course subject to my two colleagues agreeing, of utilising one of these mornings to discuss with you the Rule 98 bis procedure that will follow immediately after the Prosecution rests its case. So I welcome any suggestions that you may have in regard as to the date. The other remaining thing is, if it is at all possible, to either bring forward those witnesses that are here in The Hague and that you had scheduled as new witnesses, some at them at least, for later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may. We have no witnesses available here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm talking of the ones who would have testified about the chain of custody. I thought that they were here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. That might be a misunderstanding, but they are not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not even the military officer witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I do realise that you have a problem. You have a problem, but the Trial Chamber will try to help you out in trying to find a solution to avoid wasting an entire week -- not wasting but losing. It's not wasted. What practical suggestions or recommendations do you have, Mr. Wubben, and please do understand that you have our understanding all the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Well, we have -- we have available now at the beginning of the week the contacting possibilities with these witnesses, although various witnesses have fixed a date or lawyer -- lawyers among them who have a free agenda projected as such based upon our proposal, meaning that they have fixed dates, and others might have even additional information. We have to find out. So by the end of the day or the beginning tomorrow, we are in a far better position to confirm any opportunities. Prior to that, Your Honour, if you allow me, there is -- there is still the issue of the new-coming witness. There is an order of appearance by your Trial Chamber, an order for subpoena which includes that Witness C003 shall appear at the Tribunal on the date which will be specified further, and that the representatives of the Tribunal have to cooperate with that. So according to this order, C003 is still available, and I would advise the Trial Chamber to take a position whether or not the Trial Chamber itself wants to use its position to put questions or to inform him, or the Trial Chamber decide to leave that up to Prosecution to update this witness who is waiting here in the neighbourhood as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's suspend the sitting for a couple of minutes. We'll be back -- you don't need to leave the courtroom -- we'll be back in less than five minutes. The reason is to consult among ourselves, obviously. There's no other reason. --- Break taken at 9.17 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. -- The accused is here. Mr. Wubben, I take it -- I just want to confirm with you. I take it that your decision to withdraw this witness is an irrevocable one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you have considered, in reaching this decision, other options.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I have considered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Other options.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I have considered them but I have not come to a final opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You haven't come to a?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Final opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have come to a final opinion. This is why I'm asking you whether the decision to withdraw this witness is an irrevocable one or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Well, it's definitive, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So basically you have considered all the options that you had, including that of proceeding with the testimony of this witness, and if he becomes an adverse or a hostile witness, to proceed along the lines of asking for a declaration to that effect, and you have decided against -- or, rather, you have decided in favour of withdrawing the witness rather than proceeding the other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So having cleared that, our decision is also a very simple one. We -- it doesn't even cross our mind for a moment of calling Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the witness ourselves, and for that matter, we don't consider the need of a subpoena because a subpoena would fall in place only if there were further proceedings to follow. And I think that the matter ends there. The matter ends there. Now, how are we going to utilise the rest of the time we have this week profitably? And I need suggestions from you first, Mr. Wubben, and then from the Defence if whatever you suggest creates problems for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, today the Prosecution will try to get the information to reschedule witnesses and to try to get a witness by the last two days of this week, thus filling in at least a couple of days from the luck we have. Prior to a proposal, we will update the Defence with a view to their rights to cross-examine. And we will go through our list, as I informed you already prior this morning. It will not be easy because dates are fixed according to several agendas, but we will give that a try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm fully aware of that, Mr. Wubben, and as I said, you have our full understanding. One other matter. Witness 45, who is supposedly the one who should have followed the -- the witness we had scheduled for today, it seems to me that this is one of the new witnesses that you intend -- that you have proposed to bring forward, and to my knowledge we have not yet decided on admitting that witness. Ms. Vidovic. So at least we can decide on that witness orally today. If you have no objection on that particular witness. I'm not mentioning the name because I don't know if there are requests for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So our decision is that as regards Witness number 45, as name shown in the last confidential amended witness list presented by the Prosecution and dated the 13th of April, 2005, the Trial Chamber is authorising the Prosecution to produce that witness. So at least you have that decision in your hands. It's an oral decision, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The others we will decide, et cetera. If there is someone else that perhaps you can bring forward and who would be a new witness included in the motion that you filed a few days ago and you need clearance, authorisation from us, then do approach the Registrar after consulting with the Defence straight away so that we give clearance there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. I might be wrong, but as I recall, Defence counsel already put forward as her opinion that there are no objections --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. However, there is a pending on one person that -- I don't think -- need, I think, and we have withheld our decision basically because of that pending issue and also because of the other pending issue that there was regarding those three chain of custody witnesses on whether they could testify in writing and then cross-examination would be reserved. And otherwise we would have handed -- the decision basically is already prepared and typed out, it's a question of waiting for an outcome on the pending issues. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we've been considering the list just now, and we are not prepared to cross-examine Witness number 52 this week or next week, for that matter. We are dealing here with a highly complex and serious testimony which requires a longer preparation time in order to be able to cross-examine. Therefore, we would kindly ask the Prosecutor to not consider this witness for the next two days this week or next week. The possibility of this witness appearing, as well as the substance of his testimony, came up only recently, therefore we have not received any of the relevant documents in connection with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben. Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, I'm much obliged for this information because that enables us to focus, rather, on other opportunities. So it means, Your Honours, that we might contact today or tomorrow Defence counsel for further scheduling and then finally update you with an advice to reschedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you, Mr. Wubben. In the meantime, let's schedule a sitting where we will discuss Rule 98, the Rule 98 procedure that will be adopted. My suggestion to you, I of course stand -- I stand to be corrected or I would welcome any other alternatives, but I take it that by tomorrow you should more or less be in a position to know if we could utilise the remaining days of the week, at least the last two days or so. So let's try and meet Wednesday morning, deal with the Rule 98 bis. I take it -- I mean, don't expect to have this debate last more than an hour. It's pretty plain sailing, according to us. What I would like you to do is I know that the options that you may have may be quite limited, but -- I honestly don't know what to suggest because two of the witnesses that were scheduled for next week -- sorry, for the week 17th to 19th, one of the witnesses is -- was scheduled to last five hours. That's basically three days, if not more. The others were three each. Basically we're talking of two days each. But of course today is already Monday. So it's still a problem. But any day or two that we can gain will always help us a lot. And do keep in mind that the weekend starting on the 13th of May is a long weekend since Monday the 16th is a UN holiday or, anyway, it's holiday for this tribunal. So do keep that in mind. If possible, we won't -- try not to leave anyone here Friday because we won't be sitting on Friday either, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, and Monday, waiting here for nothing. So, please, I trust my hands in your organisational skills and expertise, Mr. Wubben, and I'm sure you will try and come forward with some kind of a solution. I see none for the time being because I don't know what your problems are, obviously, I mean. But I can anticipate problems in trying to airlift someone from Yugoslavia or from somewhere at 24 hours notice, except maybe with Nikola Popovic, but then you wouldn't have gained much, you know, because he was scheduled to testify here for one hour. All the other witnesses are three hours, three hours. I don't know what to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will do our best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I'm sure you will. I'm sure you will. So we will be sitting again, Madam Registrar, please, on Wednesday morning at 9.00 in this same courtroom. I think we should keep it at 9.00. We should keep it at 9.00. And then when we finish, we finish. In the meantime, if there are further problems that we need to discuss about rescheduling, obviously we'll discuss them. All right? I thank you, and I do understand that this is a problem which is certainly not self-inflicted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 4th day of May, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 9.43 a.m.,
